title: Microsequence storyboard GIFs for release notes (onboarding & quickstart flows)
creator: Ava Patel
description: Produce a set of high-quality microsequence GIFs (3–6s) to illustrate key onboarding and quickstart flows for the March 2026 changelog and release blog. GIFs should emphasize before->after UX improvements, progressive disclosure (tooltips/onboarding overlays), and a clear focal CTA. Deliverables will be used in the blog, changelog modal, and social posts.
acceptance_criteria: Five GIFs exported at 30fps, 800px width (max 1MB each when optimized), demonstrating distinct flows: first-run quickstart, API key setup, model selection, canary rollout toggle, and cost-breakdown toggle.
Each GIF has optional caption frames (0.8s) and adheres to brand motion guidelines (easing, duration).
Accessible: captions available as separate short MP4s and a 1-frame static PNG fallback for emails. Contrast and motion tested per accessibility QA.
Source Figma file and export spritesheet uploaded to Drive; production-ready assets placed in design-assets/release-2026-03.
Signoff from PM (Iris Moreno) and Motion Lead (Liam Chen) recorded in comments.
assets_required: Figma microflow frames (artboard names prefixed: GIF_RN01…GIF_RN05)
Motion easing tokens and timing palette (from design system)
Voiceover-free captions copy (3–6 words per frame), provided by content team
Export scripts for ffmpeg optimization and a suggested GitHub Action for automating GIF -> MP4/WEBP conversions
design_notes: Priority is clarity over embellishment — keep UI chrome minimal, highlight changed elements with 30% saturated accent overlays.
Use 3-step microsequences where possible: state A -> transition (0.4s) -> state B; for toggle flows include a quick hover to show intent.
Avoid long camera pans; prefer 1.1x subtle zoom for focus where needed.
Prepare a static master PNG from the final frame with annotation hotspots for marketing team to use alongside the GIFs.
export_considerations: Target max file size: 1MB GIF or fallback to MP4/WEBP for socials if GIF > 1MB after optimization.
Use ffmpeg palettegen + paletteuse for best color fidelity; provide a sample command in the ticket comments.
Deliver both GIF and MP4 (H.264 baseline) and a WebP animated for modern browsers.
Include a 72dpi PNG fallback for email clients and CTAs.

Accessibility-first transition timing inserted after QA feedback; resulted in marginally longer GIFs but safer UX.
